# Steering box swap for durability

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Mount a D21 manual steering box to the frame, slotting mount holes if necessary to reverse the angle. [t1846]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove the existing idler arm assembly from the vehicle.
2. [Partial] Mount a 1986.5-1990 D21 manual steering box to the frame, slotting mount holes if necessary to reverse the angle for left-side installation.

_Procedure reported by [t1846]._

## Tools

- Hack saw or Sawzall [t1846]
- Vice and pipe wrench [t1846]
- Punch and hammer [t1846]
- [Partial] Sockets (19mm) and wrenches (27mm) [t1846]

## Parts

- D21 Manual Steering Box: Year range 1986.5-1990 for correct spline size; avoids offsetting the idler pivot by 10mm. [t1846]
- [Partial] Pitman Arm: From a 4WD Hardbody or Pathfinder with power steering, 1986.5-1989; shorter length than 2WD manual versions. [t1846]

## Tips & gotchas

- Save the original bolts from the old box for reuse. [t1846]
- [Partial] When reassembling a disassembled D21 box, plug any shaft holes with rubber seals and fender washers filled with weld or JB Weld to prevent leaks since oil pressure is low. [t1846]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using a 4WD manual Pitman arm which is too long for the specific setup. [t1846]
- [Partial] Mounting a box with a larger spline (post-1990) without accounting for the 10mm offset in pivot geometry. [t1846]
